beats.text: Lithrim Bench. You install it, point it at your own agent — here, a clinical scribe — and bring your own key. It runs entirely on your machine.

Here is a real scribe note. You hit verify, and Bench runs a real council — three judges, across three different model providers — against four pillars: faithfulness, completeness, safety, and structure.

They unanimously block it, at full confidence, for fabricated history. But every flagged condition is real — it is in the patient's chart, a source the judges never read. A confident, unanimous panel, completely wrong.
Your instinct is to fix the judge's prompt. But that lever is non-monotonic — we measured it; the stricter prompt caught less, not more. Against known truth, the council scores just three out of six.

So you do not reword it — you ground it. A deterministic, zero-cost floor reads the source the judges could not, and overrules them. Accuracy against truth climbs to six out of six. That is the product: you calibrate by grounding, not by guessing.
Then you point it at your own traffic. Every verdict carries a grounded audit trail, back to the source — an eval you can defend to your team, or to a regulator.
LLM judges alone do not suffice. Lithrim Bench — calibrate your judges against a truth you can prove.
